models.name: model_a
models.label: Model A — Sensor-robust (deployed)
models.conditions: Rank within property type; pair with CO2 sensor-repair; re-audit after one season.
models.narrative: Deployed model. Sensor-robust logistic model (no CO2, no lag_temp): AUROC 0.8412, PPV 0.5855, sensitivity 0.7726 at threshold 0.51 (5-fold property-level CV, n=250). It powers the upgrade ranking. CONDITIONAL because reliability is lower for flats (AUROC 0.6784 vs 0.8295 terraced, n=70 flats): rank within property type rather than on one cross-type list.

deployment_questions.q1: At threshold 0.51 sensitivity is 0.7726; it misses ~22.7% of genuinely cold property-days (12278 of 53982 in held-out CV).
deployment_questions.q2: PPV 0.5855 — a positive flag is correct ~59% of the time.
deployment_questions.q3: NPV 0.8899 — an all-clear is correct ~89% of the time.
deployment_questions.q4: AUROC 0.8412 — ranks a cold property above a warm one ~84% of the time.
deployment_questions.q5: No — flats AUROC 0.6784 vs ~0.8295 for houses (flats are warmer: 10.5% vs ~37% cold base rate). Rank within type.
deployment_questions.q6: By design this model uses NO CO2, so the 38% MNAR dropout cannot affect it. The CO2 failures are surfaced separately as a sensor-repair flag for 40 properties.
deployment_questions.q7: A false negative leaves a genuinely cold household below 19C for another heating season — a delayed health outcome for vulnerable residents, not a calibration nicety.
deployment_questions.q8: Yes — recommended as the ranking engine, with per-type ranking and a sensor-repair workstream.

models.name: model_b
models.label: Model B — Multimodal incl. CO2
models.conditions: Do not deploy; CO2 MNAR with no lift.
models.narrative: Multimodal incl. CO2. AUROC 0.8427 — only +0.0015 vs the CO2-free Model A. CO2 is 38% missing (MNAR, 40 properties at 70-95% dropout) yet adds no predictive value, so it is a fragile dependency for no benefit. NOT READY: superseded by Model A. The CO2 sensor failures are an asset-management/repair issue, not a ranking input.

deployment_questions.q1: At threshold 0.51 sensitivity is 0.7738; it misses ~22.6% of genuinely cold property-days (12211 of 53982 in held-out CV).
deployment_questions.q2: PPV 0.5866 — a positive flag is correct ~59% of the time.
deployment_questions.q3: NPV 0.8905 — an all-clear is correct ~89% of the time.
deployment_questions.q4: AUROC 0.8427 — ranks a cold property above a warm one ~84% of the time.
deployment_questions.q6: Tested directly: CO2 adds +0.0015 AUROC and is 38% MNAR-missing. Including it makes reliability depend on a sensor that has failed for 40 properties — net negative.
deployment_questions.q7: A false negative leaves a genuinely cold household below 19C for another heating season — a delayed health outcome for vulnerable residents, not a calibration nicety.
deployment_questions.q8: No — kept only as evidence; do not deploy.

models.name: model_c
models.label: Model C — Nowcast incl. lag_temp (leakage)
models.narrative: Leakage exhibit. Adding lag_temp lifts AUROC to 0.9302 (+0.089 over Model A), and a row-level split lifts it further to 0.9316. But lag_temp is yesterday's indoor temperature — essentially yesterday's value of the target — so the gain is target leakage, not skill. NOT READY: do not deploy; always split by property and exclude lag_temp.

deployment_questions.q1: At threshold 0.43 sensitivity is 0.8905; it misses ~11.0% of genuinely cold property-days (5909 of 53982 in held-out CV).
deployment_questions.q2: PPV 0.6661 — a positive flag is correct ~67% of the time.
deployment_questions.q3: NPV 0.9466 — an all-clear is correct ~95% of the time.
deployment_questions.q4: AUROC 0.9302 — ranks a cold property above a warm one ~93% of the time.
deployment_questions.q6: Not the failure here — this model's problem is lag_temp leakage, not CO2.
deployment_questions.q7: A false negative leaves a genuinely cold household below 19C for another heating season — a delayed health outcome for vulnerable residents, not a calibration nicety.
deployment_questions.q8: No — kept only as evidence; do not deploy.

overall_notes: CONDITIONAL. Temperature/humidity/smart-meter reliable; CO2 MNAR (38% missing, 40 properties >=50% dropout) but uninformative; resident survey ~97% missing (MNAR). Property-level split verified (0 cross-fold overlap); lag_temp excluded as target leakage. Deploy Model A with within-type ranking; commission CO2 sensor repairs; re-audit after one heating season.

content.reranking_under_fair_weighting: A single cold-risk list ranks houses above flats because flats are genuinely warmer (10.5% vs ~37% cold) — correct, not bias. If the budget should reach the coldest homes of every stock type, within-type allocation adds 14 flats the global top 50 omits. The council should choose 'coldest absolute' vs 'coldest per type' explicitly.

threshold_sensitivity_report.sensitivity_fatigue_tradeoff: At a 0.5 dropout cut-off, 40 properties are flagged for sensor repair — the natural break (the MNAR cohort sits at 70-95%). 0.3 flags 140 (review fatigue); 0.8 flags 24 (misses borderline-failing sensors).

fairness_disparity_summary.recommended_mitigation: Flag-rate differences across types reflect true cold differences, not unfairness. The real fairness risk is lower model reliability for flats (AUROC 0.6784). Mitigate with per-type ranking/thresholds, surface a reliability flag in the UI, and repair CO2 sensors so the data improves for the under-instrumented cohort.
